messages:
From: Diego Fernández <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Candidate 3 — clarifying notes and rapid consensus

Hi team,

Thanks for the quick debriefs this morning. I pulled everyone's raw scorecards and the short notes into one doc (linked below) and attached the candidate scorecard + resume for reference. We still have a bit of qualitative divergence on two areas: system design depth and ownership examples.

Ask: can we close this out with a 24-hour rapid consensus? Two small asks:
- Please add any short clarifying notes to the Google doc (link below) by end of day tomorrow. One-liners are fine — e.g., "strong design tradeoffs, weak infra ownership example."
- Cast a quick vote in the HubSpot poll I created: Approve for hire / Keep for callback / No hire. If you need to change a numeric score, note the delta in the doc (e.g., +1/-1).

I've attached the aggregated scorecard (candidate-3-scorecard.pdf) and the resume. If you want to attach your annotated scorecard, please reply to this thread so I can collect them centrally.

Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aCandidate3-notes (qual notes)
Quick vote: https://poll.hubspot.com/df/quick-vote-ethan-morales

Thanks — aiming to freeze the decision by Friday EOD. If there's a blocker, flag it here and I'll call it out.

Diego
Diego Fernández
Staff Recruiter (Talent Ops)
Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks for the doc. I uploaded an annotated scorecard (annotated-scorecard.xlsx stub) with three short comments inline. Main concern: candidate's infra ownership seems transactional — I want to see concrete SLO/incident examples. That said, the system design answers were very good and show pattern recognition.

Vote: Keep for callback — if we can get a 45–60 minute deep-dive specifically on reliability/incident playbook, I think they can clear the bar. If you prefer binary, then No hire today.

I also suggested a minor weighting tweak in the attached (increase ownership weight from 0.2 -> 0.3) — this changes the weighted score by -0.4.

Logan

Senior Staff SWE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Candidate 3 — clarifying notes and rapid consensus

Diego — consolidated note below (merging everyone's bullets and Logan's annotated scorecard):

-- merged narrative --
Candidate shows strong system-design instincts (pattern recognition, tradeoffs, latency-aware architecture). Ownership evidence is mixed: documented a migration project but limited follow-up metrics or incident leadership. On culture fit, candidate aligned well with cross-functional communication expectations.

Tally (quick vote): Approve for hire — 2 (Mina, Marissa)
Keep for callback — 1 (Logan)
No hire — 0

Weighted score after Logan's suggested weight change: 7.4 / 10 (aggregate). If we treat Logan's ask as a blocking item, we should call a technical callback focusing on reliability and incident response. Given the votes, my recommendation: proceed to callback for a targeted reliability deep-dive (45–60 mins) rather than extend an immediate offer.

Diego — can you please schedule the callback for next week and include a short brief for the interviewer (notes attached)? If anyone strongly disagrees with the recommendation, reply-all with objections within 24 hours; otherwise I'll consider this consensus.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Hiring Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: callback-brief.pdf (generated from merged notes)
